summary.text: A 72-year-old man was referred to the hand clinic by a spine surgeon for extension impairment of the left thumb and fingers. He had undergone posterior cervical decompression for distal-type cervical spondylotic amyotrophy with C8 involvement one year earlier, and the C6/7 cord compression was resolved but extension impairment persisted.

When he visited the clinic, abductor digiti minimi atrophy was evident. Manual muscle testing graded wrist flexion 4, finger MP extension 2–3 and thumb extension 0–1, with extension lags of the thumb and ring and small fingers and no sensory disturbance. Left pinch was 7.5 kg; left grip was 30 kg, which the authors called reduced; DASH-JSSH was 30. MRI at the initial hand clinic visit showed high signal intensity in the finger extensor mass and FCU.

Because wrist flexor strength was acceptable but MRI showed FCU signal change, the brachioradialis tendon was chosen as donor and transferred to the EPL and EDC tendons by the Zancoli method with fascial release. The wrist was splinted in extension for four weeks postoperatively, a sling was used in postoperative week 1, active mobilization began on postoperative day 1, and he underwent rehabilitation.

At two years postoperatively the extension lags of the 4th and 5th MP joints and thumb had improved, with slight wrist flexion during finger extension. The DASH-JSSH score improved from 30 to 11.6 following surgery, MHQ-J scores improved, grip strength showed no significant change, and the patient regained the ability to open the hand.
